newsitem.title: UK: Stocks rise sharply in Tokyo, edge up in London.
newsitem.headline: Stocks rise sharply in Tokyo, edge up in London.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Wednesday.

LONDON - British shares were firm at the close, underpinned by fresh gains in the Dow and U.S. Treasury bonds. After touching a record 4,466.5 in early trade, the FTSE 100 coasted lower for much of the day to close up just 2.8 points at 4,436.0 -- short of the record close of 4,444.3 set March 11.

FRANKFURT - German shares bounded higher in bourse trade in a delayed response to post-bourse gains from Tuesday when benign U.S. data were seen as reducing the imminent need for a U.S. interest rate rise. The DAX-30 index of leading German shares ended the session up 54.88 points, or 1.6 percent, at 3,438.07, some 14 points off its session high of 3,452.61. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 3,438.09. up 12.23.

PARIS - French shares closed sharply higher in big volume boosted by options expirations. The Bourse, which is closed on Thursday for the May Day holiday, started with a 1.47 percent gain, building on Tuesday's 2 percent advance due to a jump on Wall Street as data on labour costs and durable goods dispelled inflation fears. The CAC-40 index closed up 1.41 percent at 2,639.46, a rise of 36.60 points.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended at a record high after overcoming a brief period of temporary weakness that followed the afternoon release of U.S. GDP data. The Swiss bourse will be closed on Thursday for the Labour Day holiday. The Swiss Market Index (SMI) was up 42.5 points, or 0.88 percent, to 4,897.6. The Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 23.70 points, or 0.77 percent, to 3,094.65.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks surged upwards, with the key index ending up nearly 500 points at its highest close in four months. The rally was inspired by a surge on Wall Street on Tuesday and the yen's weak trend against the dollar. Plans by a number of firms to buy back their own shares, announced in recent weeks, also brightened the market. The Nikkei average of 225 leading shares ended up 480.75 points or 2.57 percent at 19,151.12.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks posted their biggest point gain in more than two months after U.S. economic data calmed fears about higher interest rates and triggered an overnight surge on Wall Street. The blue chip Hang Seng index jumped 302.88 points, or 2.40 percent, to close at 12,903.30.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market reached new peaks before an avalanche of profit-taking wiped out most of the early gains. The All Ordinaries index added 8.9 points to 2,488.0 after touching a record high of 2,515.1 shortly after the market opened. This surpassed the previous record high of 2,508.3 reached on Feb. 19.

JOHANNESBURG - South African industrial shares staged a late rally as futures related buying helped shed their earlier losses to finish firmer. Gold shares sank to fresh four-year lows as woes on the weak bullion price pervaded the market. The overall index ended up 23.5 points at 7,130.5, the industrial index gained 41.5 points to 8,494.3 points and the gold index dropped 18.2 points to fresh four-year low of 1,187.0 points.
